business_process: Remote patient monitoring and secondary alarm notification
description: Clinicians view VM-7 and VM-5 telemetry remotely; the CCC sends secondary alarm notifications to hospital clinical communication systems and results to EHRs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Hospitals staff units around remote viewing and secondary notifications; primary alarms stay at the bedside and monitors buffer 72 hours locally, so 4 hours is tolerable with hospital downtime procedures; data older than 15 minutes has little clinical value; 99.9% availability commitment
manual_workaround: Hospital downtime procedures: bedside alarm response only, increased rounding; the company's clinical support line calls affected hospitals
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; hospital networks and clinical communication vendors
dependent_people_or_facilities: Site reliability engineers (on-call); clinical support line
quantified_operational_impact: About 290 hospitals and about 21,000 VM-7 plus 11,500 VM-5 monitors lose remote viewing; about 6,000 secondary notifications an hour stop
quantified_regulatory_impact: Service credits under the 99.9% commitment; a prolonged outage with a patient event is screened for MDR (21 CFR 803.50)
patient_safety_impact: Severe: delayed response to a deteriorating patient where a hospital relies on remote viewing
fda_or_contract_linkage: CCC contracts (service credits up to 25% of monthly fees); BAAs (availability of PHI); 524B(b)(2) related system

business_process: IP-4 drug library management and EHR-integrated pump programming
description: Pharmacists publish drug libraries to IP-4 pumps; orders flow from hospital EHRs to pumps for auto-programming and infusion records flow back
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Pumps keep running on the last library; without auto-programming nurses program manually, which raises the error rate; 8 hours is one nursing shift
manual_workaround: Manual pump programming with independent double-check; library updates held; infusion records charted manually
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; hospital EHR interface teams
dependent_people_or_facilities: Site reliability engineers; clinical support line; hospital pharmacists
quantified_operational_impact: About 7,800 pumps at about 140 hospitals; about 9,000 auto-programmed infusions a day revert to manual programming
quantified_regulatory_impact: Service credits; an event with a programming error is screened for MDR
patient_safety_impact: Severe: wrong-dose risk rises with manual programming

description: Nurses photograph at-risk skin through the clinician app; the CCC returns a flag and heat map for possible pressure injury
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Adjunct tool; the standard skin assessment continues without it; images taken during an outage can be queued on the hospital device for 24 hours
manual_workaround: Standard skin assessment by nurses; images queued and analyzed after recovery
dependent_people_or_facilities: Site reliability engineers; clinical support line
quantified_operational_impact: 22 hospitals; about 3,500 images a day queued
quantified_regulatory_impact: Labeling states the tool is an adjunct; no reporting clock unless a patient event follows
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: missed early flag for pressure injury
fda_or_contract_linkage: AI-001 De Novo labeling and predetermined change control plan; BAAs

description: The CCC update service stages signed VM-7, IP-4, and AI-001 releases for hospitals to install
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Routine releases can wait 2 days; an out-of-cycle fix must be distributable within 24 hours of signing because 524B(b)(2)(B) expects critical patches as soon as possible
manual_workaround: Field service installs by USB for urgent fixes; hospitals delay scheduled installs
dependent_people_or_facilities: Site reliability engineers; field service engineers
quantified_operational_impact: Hospitals install about 600 updates a day during a release window
quantified_regulatory_impact: 524B(b)(2)(A)-(B) patch availability; FDA postmarket guidance 60-day fix window for uncontrolled risk
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: delayed fix leaves a known vulnerability open
fda_or_contract_linkage: 524B(b)(2); FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (2016) section VII.B

business_process: Vulnerability monitoring, PSIRT, and coordinated disclosure
description: Match SBOMs against vulnerability sources and the KEV catalog, receive researcher and ISAO reports, triage, and coordinate disclosure
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Intake must never stop for more than a day; the 30-day customer communication and 60-day fix clocks for uncontrolled risk start when the company learns of a vulnerability; 3-business-day acknowledgment commitment
manual_workaround: Phone and ISAO portal intake; spreadsheet tracking; manual SBOM checks for KEV entries
quantified_operational_impact: About 3 external reports a month and about 60 new component vulnerability matches a week
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missed acknowledgment or late customer communication can lose the FDA enforcement-discretion path and require an 806.10 report
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: a vulnerability with uncontrolled risk stays unassessed
fda_or_contract_linkage: 524B(b)(1); FDA postmarket guidance (2016) sections VII.B and IX

business_process: Complaint handling, MDR, and correction and removal reporting
description: Record, evaluate, and investigate complaints; decide and file MDRs and 806 reports; manage CAPA
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The clocks are regulatory: 5 work days (803.53), 10 working days (806.10), 30 calendar days (803.50); losing complaint records would be a Severe regulatory impact
manual_workaround: Paper complaint forms and a spreadsheet log; phone to FDA reporting contacts if the portal is unavailable
dependent_third_parties: eQMS vendor; FDA electronic submissions gateway
quantified_operational_impact: About 140 complaints a month, about 4 MDRs a month
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: delayed recognition of a device problem

description: Build, test, sign, and publish firmware, CCC, and AI-001 releases through the CI/CD pipeline and HSM-backed signing service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every fix depends on signing; the 60-day fix window tolerates a 3-day stop, but an out-of-cycle release needs signing within 24 hours of approval
manual_workaround: None for signing (by design); builds pause
dependent_systems: SYS-04; SYS-02 (build and signing account); SYS-03
dependent_people_or_facilities: Build and release engineers; two signing approvers
quantified_operational_impact: About 95 firmware and software engineers idle or reworking; about 40 builds a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: A signing outage during an uncontrolled-risk response threatens the 60-day fix window

business_process: Design controls, PLM, and regulatory submissions
description: Maintain design history files, risk management files, threat models, and submission documents
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Submission timelines are months long; PLM exports cover urgent needs
manual_workaround: Work from exported documents; hold design reviews
quantified_regulatory_impact: Design history file completeness (820.10(c); ISO 13485 clause 7.3)

description: Surface-mount assembly, reflow, automated optical inspection (AI-003), and board test for all products
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 3 days of boards are buffered before Lines 2 and 3; lines can run 1 shift of overtime to catch up
manual_workaround: Hold lots; build from buffered boards; manual visual inspection at reduced rate if AOI is down
quantified_regulatory_impact: Production records must be complete before release (ISO 13485 clause 7.5.1)

description: Final assembly, firmware load, device certificate injection, and final test of VM-7 monitors
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $472,000 of monitor revenue a day, but 3 weeks of finished goods protect shipments; overtime recovers about 3 days of lost output
manual_workaround: Ship from finished goods; defer lower-priority orders
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (Line 2 test stations, MES, provisioning server); SYS-04 (released firmware)
quantified_regulatory_impact: None if lots are held until test records are complete

business_process: Infusion pump assembly, flow calibration, and test (Line 3)
description: Assembly, flow calibration on 12 benches, firmware load, certificate injection, and final test of IP-4 pumps
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $248,000 of pump revenue a day; 2 weeks of finished goods; calibration benches need revalidation if their software is rebuilt
manual_workaround: Ship from finished goods; hold lots
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (Line 3 benches and test stations, MES, provisioning server); SYS-04
quantified_regulatory_impact: Revalidation of rebuilt calibration software before release (ISO 13485 clause 7.5.6)
fda_or_contract_linkage: QMSR production and process validation (ISO 13485 clause 7.5.6)

business_process: Device history records and product release (MES)
description: The MES records every build, test result, firmware version, and certificate serial; Quality releases lots from these records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No lot can be released without complete device history records; lost records force quarantine and retest of lots; the MES database is backed up only nightly
manual_workaround: Paper travelers for up to 1 day; lots held until records are reconciled
quantified_operational_impact: About 120 devices a day; each day of lost records puts about 120 devices in quarantine for retest
quantified_regulatory_impact: Incomplete production records are a QMSR nonconformity and can block release
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: a unit released without complete test records

business_process: Order fulfillment, shipping, and UDI traceability (ERP)
description: Take orders, pick and ship from the distribution center, and record UDI and serial numbers by customer for recalls and field actions
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Shipments can wait 3 days; serial-to-customer records are needed to target any correction or removal
manual_workaround: Paper pick lists and a shipping log; reconcile serial numbers after recovery
quantified_operational_impact: About $720,000 of shipments a day are delayed (not lost); about $2.16 million at the MTD
quantified_regulatory_impact: 806.10(c) requires device identifiers and counts for a correction report; traceability under 820.10(b)(1)-(2)

business_process: Customer support, clinical support line, and field service
description: Hospital calls and tickets, clinical support, complaint intake, field service dispatch
process_owner: Director of Customer Support and Field Service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Support is the main complaint and incident intake channel; hospitals expect same-day response on clinical issues
manual_workaround: Phone tree to mobile phones; paper complaint forms; field engineers dispatched by phone
dependent_third_parties: Ticketing vendor; telephony provider; call-recording vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 450 calls and tickets a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Complaints received by phone must still be recorded (820.35(a))
patient_safety_impact: Moderate: delayed response to a device safety question

description: Repair, refurbish, and return devices, including VM-5 repairs
process_owner: Director of Customer Support and Field Service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Loaner pool covers about 1 week of repairs

description: Payroll, payables, receivables, onboarding and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; payments can wait several days
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the provider; manual payments for critical suppliers

business_process: Supplier management, purchasing, and incoming inspection
description: Purchase components, qualify suppliers, and inspect incoming material
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Component safety stock covers about 2 weeks for most parts
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders; paper inspection records
